narrative:
The model determined that you have a 39% chance of representing a bad credit risk. Because this probability exceeded the bank's acceptance threshold, your loan application was denied.

The three factors that most strongly influenced this outcome were your savings account status, the status of your checking account, and the overall loan amount you requested. Your lack of any known savings was the single biggest reason for the rejection. Having no savings is relatively common among applicants, yet it strongly pushed the model toward viewing you as higher risk compared with those who have even modest documented savings. Your checking account showing no balance came next; while many approved applicants also have no checking balance, in your case this still added to the impression of financial vulnerability. Finally, the size of the loan you asked for worked against you. At 7,980 DM, your request was more than twice the average amount approved applicants typically request, and this larger amount increased the model's concern about your ability to repay.

Taken together, these three elements outweighed other details such as your age, employment, or credit history, tipping the decision against approval.

You should focus on building verifiable savings, reducing the amount you plan to borrow, and ensuring your checking account shows consistent positive balances before reapplying. These steps will directly address the main reasons the model turned you down. (218 words)
